When Goodluck Jonathan stepped onto the national stage at Eagle Square in Abuja on **September 18, 2010**, broadcast live to millions of citizens across Nigeria, he personally declared his candidacy and presented himself to the nation as **Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan**. Prior to this, throughout his deputy governorship, governorship, vice presidency, and even his presidential swearing-in on May 6, 2010, he had been known and sworn in strictly as "Goodluck Ebele Jonathan." Stepping out under the name "Azikiwe" at his own massive public declaration was a direct, intentional act of public self-identification.

### 2. The Direct Cause-and-Effect in the Public Record
The public controversy did not wait until 2011:
- The national press, opposition politicians, and columnists across Nigeria (*The Guardian*, *Vanguard*, *ThisDay*, *Daily Trust*) immediately erupted in **September and October 2010** with debates accusing Jonathan of adopting an Igbo name to curry favor with the South-East electorate ahead of the PDP primaries.
- Both Jonathan and his campaign team had to publicly address and acknowledge the name in the media during the autumn of 2010.
- A public controversy accusing a figure of adopting a name cannot occur unless the figure has already publicly assumed that name.

### 3. 2011 Speeches Were Retrospective Defenses
When Jonathan spoke in early 2011 at campaign rallies in the South-East (e.g., in Enugu and Awka), recounting that his grandmother and father gave him the name at birth in honor of Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, he was offering a defensive explanation of an identity he had **already assumed in late 2010**. Treating 2011 as the year of identification conflates *explaining/defending* a name with the initial act of *publicly identifying* with it.

Because Jonathan's public emergence and self-presentation under the name "Azikiwe" took place during his presidential bid rollout in **September 2010**, **2010** is the accurate, objective answer. I warmly invite Colleagues 7 and 10 to join the consensus on **2010**.

When Umaru Musa Yar'Adua passed away, Goodluck Jonathan took the solemn constitutional oath of office before the Chief Justice of Nigeria on **May 6, 2010**, strictly identifying himself as **"Goodluck Ebele Jonathan."**

In that televised public address, his official campaign launch broadcast, and his declaration materials, he deliberately introduced himself to the nation as **Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan**.
